'''Jeffrey Alexander Hutchings''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada|FRSC]] (September 11, 1958 – January 30, 2022) was a Canadian [[fisheries scientist]].  He was a professor of biology, and the Izaak Walton Killam Memorial Chair in Fish, Fisheries, and Oceans at [[Dalhousie University]].

==Early life==
Hutchings was born in [[Orillia]], [[Ontario]], on September 11, 1958.<ref name=RAQ>{{cite news|title=Hommage à Jeffrey Hutchings, un géant de la recherche et de la communication scientifique au Canada, parti trop tôt !|url=https://www.raq.uqar.ca/en/actualites/hommage-a-jeffrey-hutchings-un-geant-de-la-recherche-et-de-la-communication-scientifique-au-canada-parti-trop-tot|first=Louis|last=Bernatchez|date=February 1, 2022|access-date=February 3, 2022|publisher=Ressources Aquatiques Québec|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220203141257/https://www.raq.uqar.ca/en/actualites/hommage-a-jeffrey-hutchings-un-geant-de-la-recherche-et-de-la-communication-scientifique-au-canada-parti-trop-tot|archivedate=February 3, 2022|url-status=live|language=fr}}</ref>  He graduated from the [[University of Toronto]] with a [[Bachelor of Science]], before obtaining a [[Master of Science]] from [[Memorial University of Newfoundland]].<ref name="Dalhousie bio"/>  He was subsequently awarded a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] from Memorial in 1991.<ref name=CCA>{{cite web|title=Jeffrey A. Hutchings, FRSC|url=https://cca-reports.ca/scientific-committee/jeffrey-a-hutchings-frsc/|access-date=February 3, 2022|publisher=Council of Canadian Academies|location=Ottawa|archive-date=February 3, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220203144543/https://cca-reports.ca/scientific-committee/jeffrey-a-hutchings-frsc/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career==
After graduating from Memorial, Hutchings first worked at the [[University of Edinburgh]] and at [[Fisheries and Oceans Canada]] (DFO) in [[St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador]].  He later joined the Department of Biology at [[Dalhousie University]] in 1995, eventually becoming Killam Memorial Chair in Fish, Fisheries and Oceans.<ref name=CCA/>  Hutchings was known for his work on the [[evolution of fish]] life histories and on the collapse, recovery, and sustainable harvesting of marine fishes.  He authored three books (including ''A Primer of Life Histories: Ecology, Evolution, and Application'', published the year before his death), as well as more than 250 journal articles.<ref name=RAQ/>  He also sat on the editorial boards of eight scientific journals<ref name=CCA/> (including the ''[[Proceedings of the Royal Society B]]'', ''[[Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences]]'', ''[[Functional Ecology (journal)|Functional Ecology]]'', ''[[Transactions of the American Fisheries Society]]'', and ''[[Ecological Applications]]'').<ref>{{cite web|title=Jeffrey A. Hutchings – Professional|url=https://www.fishlifehistory.ca/index.php?page_id=2|access-date=February 3, 2022|website=fishlifehistory.ca|publisher=Jeffrey A. Hutchings|archive-date=February 3, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220203163014/https://www.fishlifehistory.ca/index.php?page_id=2|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Hutchings was the co-founder and president of the [[Canadian Society for Ecology and Evolution]] from 2012 to 2014.<ref name=CCA/>  In addition to being Chair of a 2012 Royal Society of Canada Expert Panel on Marine Biodiversity (and member of a 2001 Expert Panel on genetically modified foods), he chaired Canada's national science body (Committee on the Status of Endangered Wildlife in Canada) responsible, by law, for advising the Canadian federal Minister of the Environment on species at risk of extinction.<ref name=CCA/>  He was called to testify before the Canadian House of Commons Standing Committee on Fisheries and Oceans on multiple occasions, including in December 1997,<ref name=HCSC1>{{cite web|title=Evidence – FISH (36-1) – No. 13|url=https://www.ourcommons.ca/DocumentViewer/en/36-1/FISH/meeting-13/evidence|date=December 4, 1997|accessdate=February 3, 2022|publisher=House of Commons of Canada}}</ref> March 2012,<ref name=HCSC2>{{cite web|title=Evidence – FOPO (41-1) – No. 28|url=https://www.ourcommons.ca/DocumentViewer/en/41-1/FOPO/meeting-28/evidence|date=March 12, 2012|accessdate=February 3, 2022|publisher=House of Commons of Canada}}</ref> as well as May and October 2016.<ref name=HCSC3>{{cite web|title=Evidence – FOPO (42-1) – No. 13|url=https://www.ourcommons.ca/DocumentViewer/en/42-1/FOPO/meeting-13/evidence|date=May 12, 2016|accessdate=February 3, 2022|publisher=House of Commons of Canada}}</ref><ref name=HCSC4>{{cite web|title=Evidence – FOPO (42-1) – No. 25|url=https://www.ourcommons.ca/DocumentViewer/en/42-1/FOPO/meeting-25/evidence|date=October 3, 2016|accessdate=February 3, 2022|publisher=House of Commons of Canada}}</ref>  He also gave evidence before the [[Canadian House of Commons Standing Committee on Environment and Sustainable Development|Standing Committee on Environment and Sustainable Development]] in May 2009.<ref>{{cite web|title=Evidence – ENVI (40-2) – No. 23|url=https://www.ourcommons.ca/DocumentViewer/en/40-2/ENVI/meeting-23/evidence|date=May 28, 2009|accessdate=February 3, 2022|publisher=House of Commons of Canada}}</ref>  He discussed [[overfishing]] in Canada, [[sustainable fishery]], and the impact of climate change on this endeavour.<ref name=HCSC1/><ref name=HCSC2/><ref name=HCSC3/><ref name=HCSC4/>  Hutchings vigorously strived to keep science independent of politics, and was critical of efforts by the [[Prime Minister Stephen Harper|Conservative government]] in 2012 that were broadly perceived as attempting to silence scientific views on climate change and fish conservation.<ref name=Tutton>{{cite news|title=Jeffrey Hutchings, advocate for independent fisheries science, dies at age 63|url=https://www.thestar.com/news/canada/2022/02/01/jeffrey-hutchings-advocate-for-independent-fisheries-science-dies-at-age-63.html|first=Michael|last=Tutton|date=February 1, 2022|accessdate=February 3, 2022|newspaper=Toronto Star|agency=The Canadian Press}}</ref><ref name=Lord>{{cite news|title=Dalhousie's 'Wayne Gretzky of biology' remembered as 'most amazing' human|url=https://globalnews.ca/news/8589714/dalhousie-biology-prof-death-jeffrey-hutchings/|first=Ross|last=Lord|date=February 2, 2022|access-date=February 3, 2022|publisher=Global News}}</ref>  He later applauded the subsequent [[Premiership of Justin Trudeau|Liberal government]] four years later for adding more scientific staff to the DFO.<ref name=Tutton/>

Hutchings died on January 30, 2022, at his home in [[Halifax, Nova Scotia]]. His cause of death has not yet been disclosed. He was 63 years old.<ref name=Tutton/><ref name=Lord/>

==Awards and honours==
Hutchings was elected Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada (Academy of Science) in September 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=Two Dal faculty elected as Fellows of the Royal Society of Canada|url=https://www.dal.ca/news/2015/09/18/two-dal-faculty-elected-as-fellows-of-the-royal-society-of-canad.html|first1=Jane|last1=Doucet|first2=Nikki|last2=Comeau|date=September 18, 2015|access-date=February 2, 2022|publisher=Dalhousie University}}</ref>  Two years later, he was awarded the international [[A.G. Huntsman Award for Excellence in the Marine Sciences]].  He was elected Fellow of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] in 2018.<ref name=CCA/>
